records.name: Garden Court Community Association
records.summary: A registered community association for the Garden Court neighborhood in West Philadelphia, active since the mid-1950s on neighborhood problems, housing and local gardens. Its news includes park cleanups, a school garden donation, and plant and vegetable giveaways.
records.what_you_do: Join or renew your membership, sign up for a park cleanup or plant giveaway, or serve on a committee such as greening, public safety, or communications. Members vote in board elections at the June annual meeting.

schedule.text: Neighborhood cleanups and plant giveaways have been held in spring. The annual meeting is on a Saturday in June, 1:30 to 3:30 pm.

cost.text: Yearly dues are $10 for an individual, $15 per family, and $35 for a business, per a June 2026 local news post. The association's own pages do not list amounts.

requirements.gear: None needed: gloves and tools are supplied at cleanups.

first_step.how: Sign up through the registration link on the next park cleanup post, or email membership@gardencourtca.org to ask how to join.
first_step.basis: Cleanups and the annual meeting are public, and the membership committee answers questions by email. The site does not say whether people from outside the area can join.
first_step.what_to_expect: A cleanup lasts about two hours on a Saturday afternoon, with paths cleared, leaves and litter picked up, and flowers planted at Barkan Park. Organizers provide gloves, tools, and refreshments. The June 2026 annual meeting was free, with food and drinks, speakers, and board votes.
first_visit_tips: Gloves and tools are provided, so there is nothing to buy.
Cleanups run 2 to 4 pm on a Saturday, so plan for that afternoon.
The June 2026 annual meeting was held at West Philadelphia Mennonite Fellowship, 123 South 51st Street, 1:30 to 3:30 pm.
Check the news page for the next cleanup date, since posts show months but not years.

records.notes: The association's own posts carry months but no years, so the newest dated evidence is third party: a WestPhillyLocal post dated June 10, 2026, and a June 8, 2026 forward on the SpruceHillCA neighbors list, both about the June 13, 2026 annual meeting. The news archive headings reportedly show September 2026, but the posts did not confirm that, so it is not used. Membership committee email membership@gardencourtca.org and president@gardencourtca.org are on the get-involved page; the record holds one email, so info@ stays. Dues come only from the two third-party pages. Non-resident eligibility is not stated. The tier 1 sign_of_life_url (an ArcGIS data layer) was replaced. The two third-party pages were read beyond the six page allowance for the group's own site.

records.name: Georgia E. Gregory Interdenominational School of Music
records.summary: A faith-based music and dance school on West Allegheny Avenue, founded in 1999. It teaches piano, voice, guitar, drums, strings, handbells, and dance to children, teens, and adults, and runs a summer camp for ages 6 to 13.
records.what_you_do: Take private or group lessons on an instrument or in voice, join a dance class such as praise dance or hip hop, or enroll in the summer music camp.

schedule.text: Weekly classes run September to June. Praise dance and hip hop meet Saturday mornings, piano and percussion meet Tuesday and Wednesday afternoons, and voice meets Wednesday afternoons.

cost.text: Lessons are charged by the hour or half hour and paid in advance. There is a one-time $25 registration fee, and the school says scholarships and subsidies are available.

first_step.how: Call (215) 430-0435 or email gegisom@aol.com to ask about enrolling, the $25 registration fee, and which class times are open.
first_step.basis: Enrollment is by phone or email, lessons are paid in advance after a $25 registration fee, and the site does not describe a trial lesson or a beginner policy.
first_step.what_to_expect: Private lessons run 30 or 60 minutes. Group classes such as strings and dance meet weekly on set days through the school year. The site does not describe a trial lesson, so ask about one when you call.
first_visit_tips: Ask about the one-time $25 registration fee and whether a scholarship or subsidy applies.
Lessons are paid in advance, so ask how payment works before you start.
Classes can be in person or on Zoom, so ask which format a class uses.
The events page lists an open house in September, so call to check this year's date.

records.notes: The events page is a calendar that mostly shows no year. Only the January to March session heading shows 2026, so that is the sign of life. The open house (September), the free student recital (June 6), and the summer camp (June 15 to July 31, ages 6 to 13) are dated events and are kept out of the schedule text. The holiday closure line gives 2025 and a 2027 end year that looks like a typo; not used. The contact page lists two emails, gegisom@aol.com (kept) and gegisom3@gmail.com; the owner should confirm which is current. Tier 1 said the school trains musicians for churches; the site does not say that, so it is removed from the summary. Dance tags added for praise dance and hip hop; ballet has no exact tag. No nearest SEPTA stop is named on the site and the address does not clearly put a stop on the same block, so none is given. The work-with-us page says the school seeks performing artists and administrative staff; no volunteer roles or background checks are described.

records.name: Germantown Community Broadcasting
records.summary: The community radio station for Germantown, on the air as G-Town Radio at 92.9 FM (WGGT-LP). It airs local music and talk shows, posts podcasts, and runs an artist residency with public gatherings.
records.what_you_do: Tune in online or on 92.9 FM, follow the podcasts, or come to public gatherings tied to the artist residency. Ask the station by email or phone how to help with its programs.

schedule.text: Shows run around the clock: overnight playlists, then host-led music, talk and podcast shows from early morning through evening. Public gatherings are announced on the news page.

cost.text: The site lists no prices for listening, events or membership.

first_step.how: Listen at gtownradio.com, then email info@gtownradio.com or call 215.609.4301 to ask how to volunteer.
first_step.basis: The station publishes a volunteer email and phone line and a newsletter sign up, and its public gatherings are open to anyone, but no roles, training or application steps are described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most people first meet the station through a show or podcast online. The site lists no visiting hours or open house, so email before you stop by the station at 24 Maplewood Mall.
first_visit_tips: Listen to a show or two online first to hear the station's style.
Watch the news page for public gatherings and window installations.
The site offers a pop-out player and listening apps such as TuneIn.

records.notes: A few entries on the shows page look inconsistent (some block end times), so the schedule text stays general. The page does not say which shows are live, so the word live is not used. The events page says nothing is scheduled. The newest dated item is an August 31, 2026 news post about the first of three gatherings; the post gives no event date or place. Tier 1 said three gatherings were announced for August 2026; that is corrected, because August is the post date. The Artist in Residence post (January 20, 2026) asks for proposals for window installations, three artists a year, four-month residencies. The contact name James Bear appears in IRS and NCCS filings but not on the station site, so the station manager named on the contacts page is used instead; the office manager is Lauren DeLucca. drop_in is not set: the site lists no visiting hours and does not say whether a listener can just show up. Tier 1 paired zines_media with neighborhood-civic, which does not list it; the interest now sits under books-writing as well.

records.name: Germantown Community Fridge
records.summary: Neighbors who keep two free community fridges stocked in Germantown. They take donations, make sandwiches, clean the fridges, and tend a small garden in warm months.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for fridge cleaning shifts, make sandwiches for grab and go drop offs, pick up donations by car, do a grocery run (up to $100, reimbursed), or help in the garden on High Street from spring through fall.

schedule.text: The fridges are open 24 hours a day, every day. Cleaning shifts are booked on a SignUpGenius sheet, and the garden runs from spring through fall.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer Google Form linked from the group's site, or email germantownfridge@gmail.com. For a cleaning shift, pick a slot on the SignUpGenius sheet.
first_step.basis: Anyone can fill in the public volunteer form, and the group contacts you afterward. The site does not describe training, orientation, or a first shift.
first_step.what_to_expect: The fridges are open around the clock and self-serve, so anyone can take food without signing up. Volunteers fill in the form first, and the group reaches out before you start a role such as cleaning, sandwich making, pickups, or the garden.
first_visit_tips: Bring labeled meals or sealed food; unlabeled meals and opened food are turned away.
Donation pickups need a car and free time, so mention your car on the form.
Grocery runs are reimbursed up to $100.
Cleaning shifts are on a SignUpGenius sheet, so book one there.

records.notes: The calendar page is empty. The only date on the group's own pages is a 2024 copyright footer, which is not evidence, so status and last_sign_of_life are carried from the tier 1 citycast article. The garden sits behind FUMCOG on High Street; FUMCOG and Germantown Kitchen Garden are in leads_only. The batch file lists kind network; the group file says program, and program is kept. Tier 1 set drop_in true; this pass sets it to false, because volunteering runs through the form and the group contacts you afterward. The FAQ does not mention grocery run reimbursement; that comes from the get-involved page. Hours are 24/7 with no other hours given.

records.name: Germantown Historical Society
records.notes: Hidden for an owner decision. The society's About page (germantownhistory.org/about.htm, read 2026-10-08) says that in 2012 the boards and memberships of the society and Historic Germantown voted to merge into Historic Germantown: Freedom's Backyard, and that the library, museum and programs continue at 5501 Germantown Ave. Under the defunct rule this is hidden. The owner or orchestrator should decide between keeping it hidden or publishing the merged name as its own record. Facts for that decision: library visits are by appointment (library@germantownhistory.org or 215-844-1683 ext. 104); the museum is closed for installation with no new hours posted (page undated); admission is free; parking behind the building is free; the society's own pages show no 2025 or 2026 dated item (copyright 2008 to 2024 only). historicgermantownpa.org is a partnership site for about 20 Northwest Philadelphia historic sites, with 2026 events and a volunteer produce share at Home Farm Club at Wyck, and it lists the society as a partner attraction; it was read but not turned into a record. The tier 1 sign_of_life_url points to that partnership site, so it is not evidence of this society's own activity.

records.name: Girl Scouts of Eastern Pennsylvania
records.summary: The Girl Scout council for Philadelphia and eight nearby counties. Girls join troops, and adults lead a troop, help one, or take council roles such as committee member or awards mentor.
records.what_you_do: Girls join a troop, or register as an individual member if no troop fits. Adults can start a troop, help an existing troop with skills, the cookie program or chaperoning, share first aid or outdoor skills, join a council committee, or mentor girls working toward the Silver and Gold Awards. Adult volunteers must be 18 or older.

schedule.text: Every troop chooses its own meeting time and place, so ask the troop leader or compare troops with the Find a Troop search on the council site.

cost.text: Girl members pay $25 a year and adult members pay $30 a year. The membership year runs from October 1 to September 30.

first_step.how: Use the Find a Troop search on gsep.org to get a list of troops near you, or fill in the volunteer interest form. Adults who want to lead a troop can start with the leader interest form.
first_step.basis: A girl pays the yearly membership and joins a troop before she sees a meeting, and the site does not say whether a visit is allowed. Adult volunteers must clear state checks before a role is approved.
first_step.what_to_expect: Girls join a troop after paying the yearly membership, and each troop sets its own meeting times and place. Adult volunteers complete a state compliance packet (police, child abuse and FBI checks) and two online courses before a role is approved.
first_visit_tips: Ask the troop leader whether a girl can visit one meeting before joining.
Adult volunteers have 30 days after choosing a role to finish the compliance steps.
Gather the 3 to 4 compliance documents before starting, since partial submissions cause delays.
Compliance questions go to memberservices@gsep.org with 'Compliance' in the subject line.

records.notes: Membership fees ($25 girls, $30 adults) come from the join page, which shows the membership year from October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027. The clearance page says all volunteers complete the PA Act 153 steps (police, child abuse and FBI checks); that is recorded as act153_clearances and background_check true. The fee for the clearance process is not stated. The adult minimum age of 18 is carried from tier 1; the pages read this run do not restate it. The troop volunteer page lists co-leaders, a product program manager, a treasurer and troop helpers; a new troop needs two approved adult volunteers and a meeting place. An October 15 info session is listed with no year and is not recorded. The site has no FAQ. The newcomer rating is set to 2 (tier 1 had 3) because the membership fee and clearance come before a troop visit and the site does not say whether visits are allowed. The memberservices address is added as the contact email for compliance questions.

records.name: Girls on the Run Philadelphia
records.summary: A seasonal running program for girls in 3rd to 8th grade that builds social, emotional, and physical skills through running and group talks, led by trained volunteer coaches.
records.what_you_do: Girls join a 3rd to 5th grade team or a 6th to 8th grade team for a 10-week season that ends in a 5K. Adults coach a team, high school students can serve as junior coaches, and volunteers can help at the 5K or with one-time and project work.

schedule.text: Each season runs about 10 weeks with two practices a week and ends with a 5K. Team sites set their own practice days and times.

cost.text: Registration is $225 per girl each season. Families with household income under $100,000 a year can apply for a reduced fee, and a two-payment plan is offered. The fee covers a shirt, a water bottle, practice snacks, lesson materials, 5K entry and a finisher's medal.

requirements.gear: Nothing needed from girls: shoes and running clothes can be provided if a girl needs them.

first_step.how: Apply through the coach sign-up link on the program's coach page, or sign up on the volunteer page to help at the 5K.
first_step.basis: No running experience is needed to coach, and the 5K volunteer sign-up is open to anyone. Coaches must finish training and a background check before the season, and the site does not describe a visit first.
first_step.what_to_expect: Coaches lead 90-minute practices twice a week for about 10 weeks, usually in the late afternoon, using materials the program supplies. Before the season, coaches complete about 3.5 hours of online training and about 3 hours of in-person training with program staff.
first_visit_tips: Plan for about 3 hours a week of practice time, plus the 5K day.
At least one coach per team needs CPR certification, and the program can help arrange it.
Team sites are not named on the program pages, so check the locations page for where teams meet.
Junior coaches are high school students who help the coaches and serve as role models.

records.notes: The fall 2026 season is the one on the site: about 10 weeks, two practices a week, with team sites setting practice days and times. Both grade pages show a $225 fee and sliding-scale aid for households under $100,000. The 5K is at the Navy Yard. The overview and coach pages give December 6, but the FAQ says December 3 with no year; no 5K date is recorded. Team sites are not named; the locations page names the four-county service area and one office address. The coach page names Megan Briggs as program manager and says to email the address listed on that page; that address was not read, so the tier 1 email (alyssa.cepin) is kept until the owner confirms which one to publish. The batch file lists kind program; the group file says nonprofit, and nonprofit is kept. Coach background checks and training appear only on the coach page; the background_check true flag applies to the coach role. The 5K volunteer role's requirements are not stated.
